clue.text: Humdrum habitat back in power not entirely the prospect

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the shortened word for power
not entirely means the last letter of the word for power is dropped

parts.note: fuel is what powers an engine

indicators.note: back means the word for the humdrum habitat is read from right to left

parts.note: a rut is the dull routine one is stuck in

explanation.surface: A gloomy outlook on life stuck in a dreary routine without full power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humdrum habitat' reads like a dull home but means a rut; 'back' reverses it to TUR and 'not entirely' trims the fuel word to FUE.
explanation.definitionFit: What lies ahead of us is our prospect, the time still to come.

clue.text: Squander fried food

definitions.meaning: to waste, as money or time, bit by bit
a piece of fruit or meat dipped in batter and fried

explanation.definitionFit: Fritter as a verb means to waste away; as a noun, a battered fried snack.

clue.text: Nominal figure about right

indicators.note: about means the number goes round the word for right

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
OK means right, correct

explanation.surface: A notional number roughly right.
explanation.definitionFit: A token sum is merely nominal, symbolic rather than real.

clue.text: Succeed with record length in contest

indicators.note: in places the record and length inside the contest

parts.note: a race is a contest
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Taking over after a record-length win in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to take their place, to replace them.

clue.text: The minute person has time for broadcasting, BBC boss installed

indicators.note: installed means the boss is put inside the rearranged letters
broadcasting scatters the letters of the word time into a new order

parts.note: DG is the Director-General, head of the BBC

explanation.surface: A tiny presenter is given airtime once the BBC's chief has been appointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for broadcasting' turns TIME into MIET, and 'installed' puts DG in it. The BBC is Britain's public broadcaster, run by a Director-General.
explanation.definitionFit: A very small person, minute in size, was once commonly called this, now considered offensive.

clue.text: Force ripping head from stubborn hanger-on, America

indicators.note: ripping head from means the first letter of the clinging creature is torn off

parts.note: a limpet is a shellfish that clings stubbornly to rocks
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: America violently tears the head off a persistent hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripping head from' takes L off LIMPET, leaving IMPET.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or momentum that drives something on.

clue.text: Bird about to put away flower

indicators.note: about means the bird goes around the word for eat

parts.note: a grouse is a game bird
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A bird about to swallow a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: a river. The Great Ouse is a river in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use flower for a river, which flows; this is a river through East Anglia.

clue.text: Rapid bowing, lot more difficult

indicators.note: difficult letters are hard to arrange, so they are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fast bowing on the violin is much harder.
explanation.definitionFit: On stringed instruments, tremolo is the rapid back-and-forth bowing of a note.

clue.text: Turn up for Blair — how gutted, of course!

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue means the whole string reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Tony Blair was UK prime minister

indicators.note: gutted means the inside letter of how is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at how Tony Blair has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves HW from 'how'; TONY + HW is then read backwards by 'Turn up for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Why not? is an emphatic phrase of agreement, like certainly or of course.

clue.text: Restore to normality and learn music?

definitions.meaning: to get things back on track after a disaster

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means recovering after a setback; literally, a musician picks up pieces of music.

clue.text: Such is poetic, the end for many countries with extremists

parts.note: -stan ends many country names, such as Pakistan and Afghanistan
Z and A are the extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A political verse about nations ruled by radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' are the alphabet's end letters, Z and A, here written in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse grouping is a poetic unit, so it is one thing that is poetic.

clue.text: People collecting books by symbolic system

indicators.note: collecting means the people hold the books inside them

parts.note: a nation is a people
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A population gathering volumes organised by a classification scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of written symbols, as in music or mathematics, is this.

clue.text: Bull's first line to lick cow

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of Bull's

parts.note: a row is a line
to lick is to beat or defeat

explanation.surface: A bull's first move is to lick a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like the bull's mate but is the verb meaning intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, a synonym of bully into submission.

clue.text: Half submerged, despite possibly being under less than half of water

indicators.note: in a down answer, being under means the next piece comes below
less than half of the five letters of water means its first two
possibly signals that the letters can be rearranged another way

explanation.surface: Partly sunk, even though perhaps less than half underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' makes ISTDEEP; 'Half submerged' is fair because waist height is about halfway up a body.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to one's waist in water, one is roughly half submerged.

clue.text: Drunken sort keeps high in daze

indicators.note: keeps means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: up means high

explanation.surface: A drunk who stays high, wandering in a haze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' makes STOR; 'Drunken sort' reads as a drunk person, but the adjective is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupefied state is a daze, a near synonym.

clue.text: Charges are reduced by a third to split the difference

indicators.note: to split means to sit between the letters of the next word

parts.note: a tiff is a difference of opinion, a quarrel

indicators.note: reduced by a third means one of the three letters of are is lost

explanation.surface: Fees cut by a third to meet halfway in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by a third' drops one of three letters, leaving AR; 'split the difference' looks like the idiom for compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a list of fees or duties, so charges.

clue.text: Food with slight twist after starter brings illness

indicators.note: a slight twist after the first letter means one letter swaps position just past the beginning

parts.note: aliment is food or nourishment

explanation.surface: A meal with a twist after the first course makes one ill.
explanation.walkthrough: In ALIMENT the I moves ahead of the L, just after the starting A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness or minor disorder.

clue.text: Point gun: two rounds fired initially skywards, a number of shots

indicators.note: skywards in a down clue means the string reads upwards

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
a gat is a gun
two O shapes are two rounds

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of fired

explanation.surface: Instructions to aim and fire two rounds into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: E + GAT + OO + F, read upwards by 'skywards', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is a length of filmed material, made up of camera shots.

clue.text: Phone people about fever — the empty pain translates?

indicators.note: about means the phone company goes round the fever

parts.note: BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company
an ague is a fever

indicators.note: empty means the middle of the word is taken out, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: Ringing the doctor about a fever, though the pain is hard to put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain' is the French word for bread, so 'pain translates' asks for a French loaf. 'empty' leaves TE from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is French for bread, and a long French loaf is one translation of it.

clue.text: Warming drink that's black and hot

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
randy means hot, sexually eager

explanation.surface: A warm drink that is dark and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit traditionally drunk to warm one up.

clue.text: Party held for noblest of knights

parts.note: a gala is a festive party
had means held or owned

explanation.surface: A feast held in honour of the finest knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Galahad is the purest knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, Arthurian knight, is the archetype of the noblest knight.

clue.text: Catch fish circling river, though not much of one

indicators.note: circling means the catching word goes round the river

parts.note: to tickle trout is to catch them by hand

explanation.surface: Catching fish around a river, though it is a small one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to the river: a feeble stream is not much of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, weak stream of water hardly counts as a river.

clue.text: Abundance of prayer to receive God

indicators.note: to receive means the prayer takes the god inside it

parts.note: a plea is a prayer or entreaty
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A flood of prayers offered up to welcome a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or great abundance.

clue.text: Story about tot, Scottish boy

indicators.note: about means the story goes around the sum

parts.note: a lie is a story
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A tale about a toddler, a Scottish lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child but is the verb meaning to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddie is a Scots word for a young boy.

clue.text: Divine wind originally in draught

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the medicine

parts.note: a draught of medicine is a dose

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of wind

explanation.surface: A god's wind first drawn into a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is a verb: to search for water with a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine water is to dowse for it with a forked stick.

clue.text: Old rebel, man with bounty attached, cut during capture

parts.note: he refers to a man
a reward is a bounty

indicators.note: during means the cut goes into the middle of the capture

parts.note: to take is to capture
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A wanted man with a price on his head is cut down when caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake led English resistance to the Norman conquest in the 1070s, based in the Fens of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Anglo-Saxon resisted William the Conqueror, an outlaw rebel of English history.

clue.text: Stole lean dog or cat?

parts.note: to tip is to lean
a dog or cat is an example of a pet, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Asking whether a thin animal is a dog or a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb but is the noun, a scarf worn round the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippet is a long scarf or cape worn over the shoulders, a type of stole.

clue.text: Tortured head on stick

indicators.note: tortured means the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: re means on or about

explanation.surface: A severed head stuck on a pike after torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortured' turns HEAD into ADHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick to something.
